comments.author: matrss
comments.story: iPhone 16 cameras vs. traditional digital cameras
comments.why: Xerox scanner compression replaced digits like 6 with 8.
comments.text: Worse, Xerox scanners specifically meant for digitizing documents have changed text for a long time. The compression algorithm they used (I think even in the default settings) sometimes replaced e.g. 6 with 8, and similar things. See: [VIDEO] (german, but there should be news articles from back then in english as well, somewhere)

comments.author: Log_out_
comments.story: UK plan to digitise wills and destroy paper originals "insane" say experts
comments.why: Xerox scan bug as cautionary tale for digitizing archives.
comments.text: Germany scanned its national archives in with xerox stations. We will never know what numbers might have been scrambled. [VIDEO] So similar projects existed and were so disastrous that they were quietly buried. To this day if a document was xerox scanned before the Bugfix it might be nil and void in court.

comments.author: winReInstall
comments.story: Archiving official documents as an act of radical journalism
comments.why: Xerox scanners corrupted numbers in scanned archives.
comments.text: Related: [VIDEO] guy discovered that xerox workstations (like the ones to scan in government archives) corrupted numbers. Thus falsifying documents on a massive scale. Obamas "birth certificate" went through this document shredder. So distributing, non digital copies. Thats were the lasting value is.
